note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: TDA motivation -> low-perplexity extraction pipeline -> match statistics and categorization

nodes.name: TDA is important
nodes.description: Training data attribution is considered essential for transparency, debugging, accountability, privacy and fairness in LLMs.

nodes.name: Causal TDA does not scale
nodes.description: Retraining- and gradient-based TDA offers causal guarantees but its computational cost increases dramatically with model size.

nodes.name: Similarity-based TDA is scalable but approximate
nodes.description: Similarity-based TDA, including exact string matching for verbatim recall, scales well to large models but does not guarantee causal influence.

nodes.name: Hypothesis about low-perplexity sequences
nodes.description: It is hypothesized that long low-perplexity sequences indicate either degeneration or verbatim copying from training data, which the paper tests empirically.

nodes.name: Experimental setup
nodes.description: Pythia-6.9B (trained on The Pile) is prompted with 20-40 token Wikipedia quotes from 40 articles per topic over 4 topics (genetics, nuclear physics, drugs, cryptography), with 5 generations each, using top_p 0.8 and temperature 0.7.

nodes.name: Low-perplexity window definition
nodes.description: A low-perplexity sequence is a contiguous span where each token has probability at least 0.9 (log2 P <= 0.152), analyzed with sliding 6-token windows, long enough to avoid random matches.

nodes.name: Infinigram traces windows
nodes.description: Windows are matched against the training data with Infinigram, chosen over Elasticsearch for superior scalability, with c denoting the number of occurrences.

nodes.name: Only 40% of windows match
nodes.description: Surprisingly, only about 40% of low-perplexity windows have at least one exact match in the training data.

nodes.name: Topic affects match counts
nodes.description: Drugs yield many more long low-perplexity sequences, likely due to repetitive long drug names and heavy biomedical (PubMed) coverage in the Pile, while nuclear physics is likely less represented.

nodes.name: Four behavior categories by match count
nodes.description: Windows are categorized as synthetic coherence (c=0), memorization (0<c<5), segmental replication (5<=c<50) and frequently encountered text (c>=50), with arbitrary adjustable thresholds.

nodes.name: Synthetic coherence windows are coherent
nodes.description: Zero-match windows have widely varying stand-alone perplexity, including high values, yet remain coherent rather than nonsensical, so they are not degeneration.

nodes.name: Category distribution varies by topic
nodes.description: Synthetic coherence share is 62% for cryptography, 33% for drugs, 64% for genetics and 75% for nuclear physics, while frequently encountered text is 14%, 50%, 17% and 8%.

nodes.name: About 20% are reviewable
nodes.description: Around 20% of low-perplexity windows fall into memorization or segmental replication, matching few enough documents for manual review and enabling efficient attribution.

isolated_nodes.name: Model size reduces matches
isolated_nodes.description: Across the Pythia suite, increasing model size clearly reduces both the number of low-perplexity windows and their training-data matches, supporting the 6.9B choice.

isolated_nodes.name: Generation parameters
isolated_nodes.description: Temperature 0.7 gives a meaningful number of low-perplexity windows while reducing repetition, with non-zero-match fraction and stand-alone perplexity largely unchanged.

isolated_nodes.name: Prompt repetition
isolated_nodes.description: A significant fraction of matched windows partially repeats the prompt, likely due to specialized keywords in it.

isolated_nodes.name: Thresholds are gradual
isolated_nodes.description: The category thresholds likely mark gradual transitions, and high stand-alone perplexity does not reliably indicate nonsensical text, so it is unreliable as a degeneration detector.

structural_reasoning: Background on TDA motivates the pipeline; matching statistics feed the categorization and its topic-level distribution.
